issues.t: Clutch slipping or wearing out
issues.sym: Engine revs climb without the car speeding up, especially under hard acceleration, a burning smell after hard driving, or the engagement point moving around in the pedal travel.
issues.why: The V10's huge torque is hard on the clutch, and hard launches and track use wear the friction disc and pressure plate. Used buyers are told to assume a clutch may be due unless records prove otherwise.
issues.next: If it slips or smells burnt, ease off and have it inspected before the flywheel is damaged. Ask for clutch records when buying.

issues.t: Clutch slave cylinder seal failure
issues.sym: The clutch pedal feels spongy or sinks, gears grind or are hard to select, or there is fluid near the bellhousing.
issues.why: The clutch slave cylinder design on 1992-2002 Vipers is prone to seal leaks, letting fluid out and air in, so the clutch doesn't fully release.
issues.next: Check the clutch fluid reservoir. A leaking slave cylinder is usually replaced along with the clutch since the transmission must come out.

issues.t: Soft clutch pedal from leaking slave cylinder
issues.sym: The clutch pedal feels soft or is slow to come back up, and you may see a few drops of clear fluid under the transmission.
issues.why: The slave cylinder inside the transmission bellhousing can leak. If ignored, the clutch can stop working entirely.
issues.next: Get it looked at early, while the car still drives. Have a Viper-experienced shop or dealer confirm the leak source.

issues.t: Crankshaft damper bolt works loose
issues.sym: A new vibration, a wobbling crank pulley at the front of the engine, or a drive belt that suddenly comes off.
issues.why: The bolt holding the crankshaft damper (harmonic balancer) on the 8.0L V10 can loosen. Left alone, it can damage the crankshaft nose.
issues.next: Stop driving if the pulley wobbles or the belt comes off. A shop can re-torque the bolt with thread locker; pinning kits are available to stop it from coming back.

issues.t: Head gasket leaks on original gaskets
issues.sym: Coolant or oil weeping down the sides of the block, overheating, or oil and coolant mixing.
issues.why: The original composite head gaskets on these engines break down with age. Later replacement gaskets are multi-layer steel.
issues.next: Look for staining on the block below the heads. If you see coolant loss or overheating, have a cooling system pressure test and combustion leak test done.

issues.t: Erratic or hunting idle
issues.sym: The idle speed surges up and down or the engine nearly stalls at a stop.
issues.why: A partly clogged idle control valve is the usual cause on these cars.
issues.next: Have the idle control valve and throttle body cleaned or checked. It is usually a simple repair.

issues.t: Power steering pump bracket cracks and assist is lost
issues.sym: Steering suddenly becomes heavy, often with a squeal or a belt that has come off.
issues.why: The cast bracket that holds the power steering pump can crack, and the factory pulley can also fail, letting the belt come off.
issues.next: Pull over safely and check the belt. Replace a cracked bracket; stronger billet brackets and pulleys are sold as upgrades.

issues.t: Oil and fluid leaks from aging gaskets and hoses
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning oil smell, or damp gaskets around the engine.
issues.why: Early Vipers are known for gasket leaks, and the hoses, belts and seals on these older cars are now aging out.
issues.next: Have the leaks traced and replace hardened hoses and belts by age, not just mileage.

issues.t: Steering rack mounting brackets can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Steering feels loose, delayed or clunky, especially on cars driven hard or on track.
issues.why: Hard driving and track use could crack the brackets that mount the steering rack to the frame. Eventually the rack could break free. Chrysler added reinforcement gussets.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check whether recall 01V313000 was done on your car. It's free.

issues.t: Rear differential mounting bracket welds can crack (recall)
issues.sym: Clunks from the rear under hard acceleration, or unstable handling.
issues.why: On cars used for track or aggressive driving, the welds on the rear differential mounting bracket could crack and the bracket could come loose. Dealers reinforce the frame.
issues.next: Have a dealer confirm recall 01V312000 was completed, especially if the car has been tracked.

issues.t: Optional racing harness may not be strong enough (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. Applies to ACR and GT2 cars with the optional 5-point racing harness.
issues.why: The harness might not meet the voluntary FIA load specifications. Chrysler replaced it.
issues.next: If your car has the factory racing harness, ask a dealer to check recall 01V120000.

issues.t: Clunk or click from the rear driveline
issues.sym: A clunk when getting on and off the throttle, or a single click or pop from the rear as the clutch is released.
issues.why: RepairPal lists these as the most commonly reported Viper complaints. Some driveline clunk is considered normal on this car.
issues.next: If the noise is new or getting louder, have the U-joints, differential and mounts checked.

issues.t: Heat soak and damage around the side-exhaust sills
issues.sym: Lots of heat in the cabin and door sills, plus scraped, burnt or rusted paint on the rocker panels around the side exhaust covers.
issues.why: The V10 and side-exit exhaust run very hot right next to the cabin, and the low rocker panels get scraped.
issues.next: Inspect the rocker and exhaust cover area when buying. Many owners repaint or coat these panels early to protect them.

issues.t: Catalytic converter failure
issues.sym: Check engine light, poor running, a rattle under the car, or a failed emissions test.
issues.why: Some cars of this generation had catalytic converter problems.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the converters checked. Fix misfires first so new converters don't fail too.

issues.t: Window regulator failure
issues.sym: A window is slow, noisy, grinds, or won't go up or down.
issues.why: Most cars of this era used weak window regulators that break internally. An upgraded regulator became available from 2009.
issues.next: Replace the regulator, ideally with the upgraded part.

issues.t: Window drops wrong and hits the roof when the door closes
issues.sym: When you shut the door, the glass slams into the roof or top instead of tucking in, which can break the glass or damage the body.
issues.why: The windows drop slightly when a door opens. If the module that controls that loses its settings, such as after a dead battery, the glass is no longer lowered.
issues.next: After a battery has gone dead, check that the windows drop before shutting the doors. Have the window positions re-learned.

issues.t: Door hinges sag
issues.sym: The door rides low, rubs or catches on closing, pops, or the weather seal is damaged and leaks water.
issues.why: The door hinges on these cars can sag or deform over time.
issues.next: Lift the open door gently to check for play. Have worn hinges adjusted or replaced before seals and paint are damaged.

issues.t: Convertible top and seal leaks
issues.sym: Water inside the car after rain, damp carpets, or dry, brittle leather.
issues.why: The soft top fabric and the weather seals wear, tear or go missing with age.
issues.next: Check the top and seals carefully and replace damaged seals before water damages the interior.

issues.t: Oil leak from the front timing cover
issues.sym: Oil wetness on the front of the engine and drips under the front of the car.
issues.why: The front timing cover is called out as the spot to check most for leaks on these V10s.
issues.next: Have the leak confirmed and the front cover resealed before it gets onto the belts.

issues.t: Battery runs down when the car sits
issues.sym: The car won't start or cranks slowly after sitting for a couple of weeks.
issues.why: Vipers are often stored for long stretches, and the battery drains. A dead battery can also cause other problems like lost window settings.
issues.next: Use a trickle charger or battery maintainer when the car is stored.

issues.t: Airbags can deploy on their own (recall)
issues.sym: Front or side airbags or seat belt pretensioners could fire while driving with no crash. You may see the airbag warning light.
issues.why: Electrical noise could damage a part in the airbag control module. Chrysler issued recalls 12V527/13V040 and then 15V046000 to replace the module and sensors.
issues.next: Have a dealer check that all airbag control module recalls are complete. The repair is free.

issues.t: Fuel pump wiring can chafe and stall the engine (recall)
issues.sym: The engine suddenly stalls and won't restart because the fuel pump fuse blew.
issues.why: The fuel pump wiring could rub on an underbody heat shield until it shorted.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: turn on your hazard lights, hold the wheel firmly and steer to a safe spot off the road. Steering and brakes can feel much heavier when the engine or power cuts out, so press the brake harder than normal. Have it checked before you drive it again. Ask a dealer to confirm recall 03V292000 was done. They wrap the harness and cover the shield edge.

issues.t: Headlights or dash lights flicker or fail (recall)
issues.sym: The parking lights, headlights or instrument lights flicker or go out.
issues.why: The park lamp contacts in the multifunction switch could corrode. Dealers reflash the body control module software.
issues.next: Have a dealer check recall 03V388000.

issues.t: Restraint control module can fire airbags unexpectedly (recall)
issues.sym: The airbags or seat belt pretensioners could deploy without a crash.
issues.why: A fault in the occupant restraint control module could trigger them. Chrysler replaces the module.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Ask a dealer to confirm recall 19V885000 was completed.

issues.t: Early engine failure
issues.sym: Knocking from the engine, low oil pressure, or the engine failing, sometimes at low miles.
issues.why: Some earlier cars of this generation lost engines, often under warranty, possibly from rod bearing failure or debris left from manufacturing. It is considered rare.
issues.next: Ask whether the engine has been replaced and check the warranty history. Shut the engine off right away if it knocks or the oil light comes on.

issues.t: High oil consumption
issues.sym: The oil level drops between changes and you need to add oil often.
issues.why: Some 2013-2015 cars used too much oil, and Chrysler worked with owners to find and fix affected engines. The dipstick is also hard to read accurately.
issues.next: Check the oil on level ground after the car has sat, reading the stick right away. Report heavy oil use to a dealer.

issues.t: Water pump failure
issues.sym: Coolant leaks from the front of the engine, a sweet smell, or the temperature gauge climbing.
issues.why: The water pump on the last-generation Viper is reported to be prone to failure.
issues.next: Watch for coolant drips and check the level often. Replace a leaking pump before the engine overheats.

issues.t: Windows bind or hit the body
issues.sym: A window is noisy or binds, or the glass touches the body when the door closes.
issues.why: Window operation and door fit are known weak points carried over from earlier Vipers.
issues.next: Run both windows fully up and down and close the doors slowly to check. Have the glass and door adjusted.

issues.t: Seat position sensor can make airbags deploy too softly (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. The airbags may inflate with less force than intended in a crash.
issues.why: The seat position sensors could misread where the seat is. Dealers add a metal shim to fix the reading.
issues.next: Have a dealer check recall 14V529000.

issues.t: Radio software could be hacked remotely (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms.
issues.why: Security gaps in the Uconnect radio software could let outsiders reach some vehicle systems. Chrysler sent out a software update.
issues.next: Make sure the radio software update from recall 15V461000 was installed.

issues.t: Passenger airbag door can break loose (recall)
issues.sym: No symptoms. In a crash the passenger airbag door could detach.
issues.why: A bad weld on the passenger airbag chute on cars built in early January 2016. Dealers replace the upper dash panel.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check recall 16V750000.

issues.t: Driver airbag wiring can be pinched (recall)
issues.sym: The airbag warning light may come on. The driver airbag may not deploy correctly.
issues.why: Wiring for the driver airbag could be pinched on some 2016 cars. Dealers replace the airbag and clockspring.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to check recall 16V736000.
